Autoencoder-Based Drift Detection method

Source: R/dfr_aedd.R
dfr_aedd.Rd

AEDD is an unsupervised multivariate detector that compares reconstruction errors produced by an autoencoder on reference and recent windows. Because it monitors changes in the input distribution rather than classifier performance, this implementation is primarily aimed at virtual concept drift. The method follows Kaminskyi, Li, and Muller (2022) doi:10.1109/ICDMW58026.2022.00109.

Usage

dfr_aedd(
  encoding_size,
  ae_class = NULL,
  ae_params = list(batch_size = 32, num_epochs = 1000, learning_rate = 0.001,
    error_function = "mae"),
  window_size = 100,
  window_type = "sliding",
  monitoring_step = floor(window_size/2),
  criteria = "mann_whitney",
  alpha = 0.01,
  threshold = 0.01,
  target_feat = NULL
)

Arguments

encoding_size

Encoding Size

ae_class

Autoencoder constructor. When NULL (the default), daltoolboxdp::autoenc_ed is used, which requires the suggested package daltoolboxdp and its Python backend.

ae_params

Named list of arguments forwarded to ae_class, plus error_function, which selects how the reconstruction error is summarised. One of "mae" (default) or "rmse".

window_size

Number of most recent rows kept by the detector. The oldest half is the reference window and the newest half the recent window.

window_type

Window policy. "sliding" (default) keeps at most window_size rows, so both halves move with the stream. "anchored" keeps every row, which pins the reference half to the beginning of the stream and makes memory grow with the stream length.

monitoring_step

Number of rows between two consecutive checks. The default checks twice per window.

criteria

The method used to check for a drift. One of "mann_whitney" (default), "kolmogorov_smirnov", "levene", "psi", "parametric_threshold", "nonparametric_threshold" or "diff_threshold".

alpha

Significance level of the hypothesis-test criteria ("mann_whitney", "kolmogorov_smirnov" and "levene").

threshold

Drift threshold of the "psi" and "diff_threshold" criteria, compared directly against the divergence or the median error difference. It is a raw threshold, not a probability.

target_feat

Names of the columns to be monitored. NULL (the default) monitors every numeric column.

Value

dfr_aedd object

Details

The autoencoder expects inputs in the [0, 1] range. Values outside that range are clipped to it, and the detector warns the first time this happens, so the data should be normalized beforehand (for example with daltoolbox::minmax()). ae_class must be a constructor accepting the arguments input_size and encoding_size plus the entries of ae_params, whose objects implement fit() and transform().

The autoencoder is trained on the reference window the first time the window is full, and again after every drift or whenever new columns appear.

The "levene" criterion tests every reconstructed feature and combines the per-feature p-values with a Bonferroni correction, instead of looking at the first feature only.

References

Kaminskyi, D., Li, B., and Muller, E. (2022). Reconstruction-based unsupervised drift detection over multivariate streaming data. In 2022 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining Workshops (ICDMW). doi:10.1109/ICDMW58026.2022.00109
